description: We’re WorkLifeBalance, five students building MOONSHIFT, a browser game for kids 7–12. Players are B.E.E.P., a lunar robot keeping three astronauts safe through five shifts as a real 2017 solar storm (NASA DONKI data) heads their way. Every choice costs power, food or shielding. Our skills span game development (React, Three.js), 3D art, UI/UX, sound and science research, and Mission 1 already plays end to end in the browser with no install.
summary:
MOONSHIFT is a browser-based strategy puzzle where kids ages 7-12 play as B.E.E.P., a lunar maintenance robot, guiding three astronauts through a real NASA-documented solar storm (September 2017, from NASA DONKI). In 5 shifts over 10-15 minutes, players make genuine trade-off decisions: fixing life support costs power, stacking food into a radiation shelter wall means fewer meals, and calling Earth on the radio uses the shift's only free power unit.

Every number comes from real NASA/NOAA data: DONKI flare timing, GOES proton flux, and SWPC storm scales. The shielding mechanic mirrors NASA's own Orion crew protection procedure - stacking mass around the crew. No reading is invented; all data is labeled "archive, not live."

The core mechanic directly addresses the challenge brief's three design traps: no free choices (every item is used or walled), accuracy over polish (shield = mass, as in Orion), and only 3 meters to track (Power, Food, Shield). Two endings reward strategy without punishing failure. Cadet mode reads every line aloud for younger players.

Fully playable in any browser, no install, no login, 1.2 MB load. Built with React and Three.js. Unit tests cover every rule and a bot plays all of Mission 1 on each build.
details:
MOONSHIFT — A Lunar Survival Puzzle for Ages 7–12

Play as B.E.E.P., a lunar maintenance robot. Guide three astronauts through a real NASA-documented solar storm (September 2017). Five shifts, five decisions, three meters, two endings. No combat, no reflexes — just read, plan, and see the consequence.

Demo Link: https://www.moonshift.courses/

The Challenge We Solved

The brief asks: "How does a 9-year-old feel the cost of trading tonight's power for a thicker shield?" Space education either oversimplifies trade-offs or overwhelms young learners. MOONSHIFT bridges this gap by turning NASA's own Orion crew protection procedure into a puzzle a child can solve. Co-playing with a parent or teacher fosters a stronger relationship and enhances the game's educational value

Gameplay — Every Choice Has a Cost

Shift 1 · Air: Fix the ventilation pipe — fitting the spare joint costs 1 power unit, or keep it as +1 wall cell.
Shift 2 · Power: One free power unit for radio, garden, or lamp — the others wait a shift.
Shift 3 · Wall: Stack cargo, food packs, and a water tank into an 8-cell radiation shelter.
Shift 4 · Storm: Move the crew to the shelter as real archive particle data peaks.
Shift 5 · Food: Open sealed food now or keep it as shielding — 6 of 6 meals needed, or one missed.

Key cascade: Radio Earth in Shift 2 → forecast arrives Shift 3 → unlocks the water tank for the wall. Skip the radio and the wall stays weak. This is the learning.

Real NASA Data — Every Number Has a Source

NASA DONKI: The September 2017 X8.2 flare and proton storm timeline drives Shifts 3–5.
NOAA GOES: Proton flux measurements (Earth ≈ Moon) set storm intensity.
NOAA SWPC Storm Scale: Determines shield requirements.
NASA Orion Shielding Concept: The core mechanic — stacking mass around the crew.
Artemis I Radiation Findings: Inform the debrief's shielding comparison.
NASA OSDR OSD-267: ISS lettuce study gives context to the garden research objective.

All data labeled "archive, not live" with a "time sped up" tag. No reading is fabricated.

Built for Ages 7–12

• One screen, one question, ≤3 choices per shift
• Color never alone, always paired with icons for accessibility
• No timer, no red failure screen — two endings that both teach

Technical Specs

• Runs on any browser: Chrome, Firefox, Safari, Edge + mobile
• 1.2 MB initial load, 2.5s on 10 Mbps
• Zero installs, zero logins
• Built with React + Three.js (3D lunar environment, 34 custom assets)

How MOONSHIFT Meets Each Judging Criterion

Impact: Any browser, no install, read-aloud mode, and accessible to any student with internet.
Creativity: Food and water become radiation shielding (the real Orion procedure as a puzzle).
Validity: Real DONKI archive data, real physics, every rule unit-tested.
Relevance: All 5 challenge trade-offs with only 3 meters, avoids all 3 design traps the brief warns about.
Presentation: One story, one visual metaphor (the shelter wall), playable in 10–15 minutes.
